column1: # Captures a consumer does not (yet) map, with the reason.
# A row here is a DELIBERATE, REVIEWED exception: check-vocabulary.sh would
# otherwise fail on it. Adding a row is like raising a budget in
# corpus-budget.txt — it belongs in a commit message with a reason, and it
# should come back out.
# consumer<TAB>capture<TAB>why
# `textmate` rows take a FOURTH field, the scope, and record a deliberate
# AGREEMENT divergence for census.mjs --gate rather than an unmapped capture.
# check-vocabulary reads only the first two fields and matches by consumer, so
# these rows are inert there. They are kept here, not in
# queries/textmate-agreement.tsv, because that file states what MEANS THE SAME:
# putting this pair in it would assert `comment` == `keyword.operator.wildcard`,
# which is false and would let a genuine comment/wildcard confusion through.
# textmate<TAB>capture<TAB>why<TAB>scope
textmate
column3: DELIBERATE. The query paints the wildcard `_` as @comment to de-emphasise it (captures.md: "a comment; also the wildcard pattern _") — it reads as "ignore this". TextMate cannot express de-emphasis, and `keyword.operator.wildcard` is the honest static reading for Linguist/GitHub. Owner ruling 2026-08-15: keep both. Painting `_` as a comment in TextMate too would make GitHub render it as if commented out.

column1: # `family` rows — deliberate ROLE divergences for check-families.sh.
# check-vocabulary reads only fields 1-2 and matches by consumer, so these are
# inert there, exactly like the `textmate` row above.
# ⚠ The four below were filed when the gate landed (2026-08-15). Two are Emacs
# vocabulary limits and are expected to stay. Two are UNRESOLVED and awaiting an
# owner ruling — they are debt, not decisions, and should come back out.
# family<TAB>capture<TAB>why
family
column3: EXPECTED TO STAY. Emacs has no namespace face; `font-lock-constant-face` for a module name is the long-standing Emacs convention. VS Code says `entity.name.namespace` (#CB4B16 in Solarized Dark), which is more precise than Emacs can be. Not a disagreement about meaning — a vocabulary limit on one side.

column1: family
column3: ⚠ UNRESOLVED — owner ruling owed. Emacs paints plain variables NOTHING (deliberate restraint); VS Code paints every one `variable.other` = #268BD2 blue in Solarized Dark. Together with the `variable.parameter` row the two editors are almost exactly INVERTED. Remove this row once ruled.
